observation.text: European Molecular Biology Laboratory Home Directory Search EMBL International PhD Programme Unique in the world and waiting for you! Home Application Programme overview Why EMBL? Contact us Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research. EMBL is dedicated to promoting excellence in the molecular life sciences throughout Europe. To achieve this goal, we inspire and train talented young scientists to become skilled and creative future leaders in academia, industry and other sectors. The EIPP provides comprehensive interdisciplinary training, maintaining a careful balance between theory and practice, close mentoring and creative freedom, collaborative teamwork and independence. These key characteristics make the EIPP a role model, which has inspired similar programmes at research institutions throughout Europe and the world. The enriching encounter of different nationalities, the friendly and collaborative atmosphere, and the passion for science is what unites EMBL’s diverse staff and provides the ideal setting to forge long-lasting connections and make studying at EMBL a unique formative experience. Application Two recruitment rounds are organised each year across all EMBL sites. The application deadlines and all relevant information are published well in advance. Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed The next application round will open in September 2026. Programme Overview Explore the structure and content of the EMBL International PhD Programme. **Longer duration due to COVID-19 related delays. Research at EMBL Find out more about the cutting-edge Research Topics investigated across our different Research Units. The complexity of current biological research questions increasingly calls for interdisciplinary approaches. To prepare our students for this challenge, the EIPP puts great emphasis on bringing together different fields of expertise: we actively encourage candidates with backgrounds in chemistry, physics, mathematics, molecular medicine, computer science or engineering to apply and work closely with biologists to answer fundamental questions in life sciences. PHD Symposium Since its first edition in 2000, the annual EMBL International PhD Symposium in Heidelberg developed into a well-recognized and highly appreciated scientific event. It is always EMBL’s first year PhD students who take on the responsibility for the conceptual development and organization of the meeting. The symposia provide a great platform for networking and scientific exchange, featuring lectures by top-level scientists as well as plenty of opportunities for young researchers to present their work. observation.text: European Molecular Biology Laboratory Home Directory Search EMBL International PhD Programme Unique in the world and waiting for you! Home Application Programme overview Why EMBL? Contact us Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research. EMBL is dedicated to promoting excellence in the molecular life sciences throughout Europe. To achieve this goal, we inspire and train talented young scientists to become skilled and creative future leaders in academia, industry and other sectors. The EIPP provides comprehensive interdisciplinary training, maintaining a careful balance between theory and practice, close mentoring and creative freedom, collaborative teamwork and independence. These key characteristics make the EIPP a role model, which has inspired similar programmes at research institutions throughout Europe and the world. The enriching encounter of different nationalities, the friendly and collaborative atmosphere, and the passion for science is what unites EMBL’s diverse staff and provides the ideal setting to forge long-lasting connections and make studying at EMBL a unique formative experience. Application Two recruitment rounds are organised each year across all EMBL sites. The application deadlines and all relevant information are published well in advance. Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed The next application round will open in September 2026. Programme Overview Explore the structure and content of the EMBL International PhD Programme. **Longer duration due to COVID-19 related delays. Research at EMBL Find out more about the cutting-edge Research Topics investigated across our different Research Units. The complexity of current biological research questions increasingly calls for interdisciplinary approaches. To prepare our students for this challenge, the EIPP puts great emphasis on bringing together different fields of expertise: we actively encourage candidates with backgrounds in chemistry, physics, mathematics, molecular medicine, computer science or engineering to apply and work closely with biologists to answer fundamental questions in life sciences. PHD Symposium Since its first edition in 2000, the annual EMBL International PhD Symposium in Heidelberg developed into a well-recognized and highly appreciated scientific event. It is always EMBL’s first year PhD students who take on the responsibility for the conceptual development and organization of the meeting. The symposia provide a great platform for networking and scientific exchange, featuring lectures by top-level scientists as well as plenty of opportunities for young researchers to present their work. observation.title: EMBL International PhD Programme – Unique in the world and waiting for you!
headings: Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research.
Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed
observation.text: European Molecular Biology Laboratory Home Directory Search EMBL International PhD Programme Unique in the world and waiting for you! Home Application Programme overview Why EMBL? Contact us Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research. EMBL is dedicated to promoting excellence in the molecular life sciences throughout Europe. To achieve this goal, we inspire and train talented young scientists to become skilled and creative future leaders in academia, industry and other sectors. The EIPP provides comprehensive interdisciplinary training, maintaining a careful balance between theory and practice, close mentoring and creative freedom, collaborative teamwork and independence. These key characteristics make the EIPP a role model, which has inspired similar programmes at research institutions throughout Europe and the world. The enriching encounter of different nationalities, the friendly and collaborative atmosphere, and the passion for science is what unites EMBL’s diverse staff and provides the ideal setting to forge long-lasting connections and make studying at EMBL a unique formative experience. Application Two recruitment rounds are organised each year across all EMBL sites. The application deadlines and all relevant information are published well in advance. Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed The next application round will open in September 2026. Programme Overview Explore the structure and content of the EMBL International PhD Programme. **Longer duration due to COVID-19 related delays. Research at EMBL Find out more about the cutting-edge Research Topics investigated across our different Research Units. The complexity of current biological research questions increasingly calls for interdisciplinary approaches. To prepare our students for this challenge, the EIPP puts great emphasis on bringing together different fields of expertise: we actively encourage candidates with backgrounds in chemistry, physics, mathematics, molecular medicine, computer science or engineering to apply and work closely with biologists to answer fundamental questions in life sciences. PHD Symposium Since its first edition in 2000, the annual EMBL International PhD Symposium in Heidelberg developed into a well-recognized and highly appreciated scientific event. It is always EMBL’s first year PhD students who take on the responsibility for the conceptual development and organization of the meeting. The symposia provide a great platform for networking and scientific exchange, featuring lectures by top-level scientists as well as plenty of opportunities for young researchers to present their work. observation.text: European Molecular Biology Laboratory Home Directory Search EMBL International PhD Programme Unique in the world and waiting for you! Home Application Programme overview Why EMBL? Contact us Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research. EMBL is dedicated to promoting excellence in the molecular life sciences throughout Europe. To achieve this goal, we inspire and train talented young scientists to become skilled and creative future leaders in academia, industry and other sectors. The EIPP provides comprehensive interdisciplinary training, maintaining a careful balance between theory and practice, close mentoring and creative freedom, collaborative teamwork and independence. These key characteristics make the EIPP a role model, which has inspired similar programmes at research institutions throughout Europe and the world. The enriching encounter of different nationalities, the friendly and collaborative atmosphere, and the passion for science is what unites EMBL’s diverse staff and provides the ideal setting to forge long-lasting connections and make studying at EMBL a unique formative experience. Application Two recruitment rounds are organised each year across all EMBL sites. The application deadlines and all relevant information are published well in advance. Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed The next application round will open in September 2026. Programme Overview Explore the structure and content of the EMBL International PhD Programme. **Longer duration due to COVID-19 related delays. Research at EMBL Find out more about the cutting-edge Research Topics investigated across our different Research Units. The complexity of current biological research questions increasingly calls for interdisciplinary approaches. To prepare our students for this challenge, the EIPP puts great emphasis on bringing together different fields of expertise: we actively encourage candidates with backgrounds in chemistry, physics, mathematics, molecular medicine, computer science or engineering to apply and work closely with biologists to answer fundamental questions in life sciences. PHD Symposium Since its first edition in 2000, the annual EMBL International PhD Symposium in Heidelberg developed into a well-recognized and highly appreciated scientific event. It is always EMBL’s first year PhD students who take on the responsibility for the conceptual development and organization of the meeting. The symposia provide a great platform for networking and scientific exchange, featuring lectures by top-level scientists as well as plenty of opportunities for young researchers to present their work. observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Computer Science MSc London, Bloomsbury Become a computer scientist in just one year through this conversion programme and enhance your career prospects in a growing and innovative field. The Computer Science MSc teaches everything from programming to app engineering while providing opportunities to create solutions for industrial or research clients. Taught at UCL, world-renowned for computer science research, this is an exceptional place to build your foundations as a computer scientist. Evidence should be included within the application to demonstrate suitable mathematical skills (to at least Mathematics A-level standard), and analytical skills. observation.title: Computer Science MSc | Prospective Students Graduate - UCL – University College London
observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Computer Science MSc London, Bloomsbury Become a computer scientist in just one year through this conversion programme and enhance your career prospects in a growing and innovative field. The Computer Science MSc teaches everything from programming to app engineering while providing opportunities to create solutions for industrial or research clients. Taught at UCL, world-renowned for computer science research, this is an exceptional place to build your foundations as a computer scientist. UK students International students Study mode Full-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £21,500 Duration 1 calendar year Programme starts September 2026 Applications accepted Applicants who require a visa: 20 Oct 2025 – 27 Mar 2026 Applications closed Applicants who do not require a visa: 20 Oct 2025 – 28 Aug 2026 Applications close at 10am UK time Applications open Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK Bachelor's degree (or international qualification of an equivalent standard) in a subject other than computer science or information technology. This includes subfields of Computer Science such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Software Engineering, among others. Evidence should be included within the application to demonstrate suitable mathematical skills (to at least Mathematics A-level standard), and analytical skills. Although the programme is intended for those who are new to Computer Science, applicants must ensure they have standard computational thinking skills, as programming is a core part of the programme. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 2 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. observation.title: Computer Science MSc | Prospective Students Graduate - UCL – University College London
observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Computer Science MSc London, Bloomsbury Become a computer scientist in just one year through this conversion programme and enhance your career prospects in a growing and innovative field. The Computer Science MSc teaches everything from programming to app engineering while providing opportunities to create solutions for industrial or research clients. Taught at UCL, world-renowned for computer science research, this is an exceptional place to build your foundations as a computer scientist. UK students International students Study mode Full-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £21,500 Duration 1 calendar year Programme starts September 2026 Applications accepted Applicants who require a visa: 20 Oct 2025 – 27 Mar 2026 Applications closed Applicants who do not require a visa: 20 Oct 2025 – 28 Aug 2026 Applications close at 10am UK time Applications open Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK Bachelor's degree (or international qualification of an equivalent standard) in a subject other than computer science or information technology. This includes subfields of Computer Science such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Software Engineering, among others. Evidence should be included within the application to demonstrate suitable mathematical skills (to at least Mathematics A-level standard), and analytical skills. Although the programme is intended for those who are new to Computer Science, applicants must ensure they have standard computational thinking skills, as programming is a core part of the programme. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 2 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. input.title: Lena Ama Mensah — LSE Master of Public Policy statement of purpose
input.body:
I am seeking the LSE Master of Public Policy to strengthen my quantitative evaluation skills for public policy. My goal is to return to West Africa to contribute to local-government finance and social-protection policy.

My academic preparation is a First Class BA in Economics from the University of Ghana, with an overall cumulative GPA of 3.78/4.00. My relevant coursework includes Econometrics I and II, Public Finance, Development Economics, Calculus and Statistics, with grades recorded in the academic transcript.

Since September 2022, I have worked in policy and research roles. At the Accra Metropolitan Research Unit, I worked on municipal revenue, social-protection targeting and quasi-experimental evaluation. Since March 2024, I have been a research assistant at the Institute for Fiscal Studies in London, continuing work in these areas. I also co-authored a published policy brief on property-rate compliance; the title and venue are not included in the supplied materials.

The programme’s quantitative public-policy orientation fits my preparation and aims. I can contribute £10,000 from savings and am applying for scholarships and other funding. I have no disciplinary findings.

input.title: Tunde Adebayo — UCL Computer Science MSc personal statement
input.body:
I am applying to the UCL Computer Science MSc to develop my preparation for applied research in artificial intelligence and machine learning. My background is a BEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering from Covenant University, completed in 2023, with a cumulative GPA of 3.72/4.00. My transcript includes Signals and Systems, Probability and Statistics, Linear Algebra, Control Systems, Digital Signal Processing, and Data Structures.

Since January 2024 I have worked as a machine-learning engineer at GridSense Africa, where I have built load-forecasting pipelines and anomaly-detection prototypes for distribution networks. My technical work uses Python, PyTorch, embedded C, signal processing, and MLOps. My final-year project focused on edge inference for low-cost power-quality sensors, which developed my interest in applying computational methods to engineering and infrastructure problems.

I am also the author of the manuscript “Self-supervised event detection for weak distribution grids,” submitted to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid on 4 May 2026; no decision has been received. This manuscript status is reported as submitted, not accepted or published.

The MSc would help me strengthen my computer-science foundations and develop more rigorous approaches to machine learning, with the goal of progressing toward applied research and engineering work in AI. I can self-fund tuition up to £18,000 and would need financial support above that amount. I have no disciplinary history.

I recognise that my transcript does not contain a course titled Machine Learning. I therefore present my preparation through my documented programming, data, signal-processing, engineering, and machine-learning experience rather than claiming a named prerequisite course.

input.title: Amara Okafor — UCL Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD statement of purpose
input.body:
I seek doctoral research in particle physics focused on detector reconstruction, uncertainty estimation, and computational methods. My preparation combines a BSc in Physics from the University of Lagos, completed in 2024 with an overall CGPA of 4.62/5.00, and current research-assistant work at CERN OpenLab.

At CERN OpenLab, where I have worked since October 2024, I work on uncertainty calibration for charged-particle track reconstruction. My undergraduate project examined muon-background rejection using a Monte Carlo study of a compact scintillator detector. These experiences developed my interest in reliable reconstruction and quantitative uncertainty assessment. I use Python, C++, ROOT, and Geant4.

I am also a co-author of “Fast uncertainty calibration for sparse detector tracks,” submitted to Computing and Software for Big Science in February 2026. I was awarded the 2023 Faculty Research Prize.

For doctoral study, I want to deepen my ability to design and validate computational techniques for particle-physics detectors, while contributing to research on reconstruction, uncertainty estimation, or closely related computational methods. I require full tuition support and a living stipend and therefore wish to be considered for relevant funding opportunities.

All factual statements above are grounded in my CV, transcript, employment history, and goals note. No formal disciplinary finding has been reported.

input.title: Tunde Adebayo — ETH Zürich MSc Data Science statement
input.body:
I am applying to the ETH Zürich MSc Data Science because I want advanced training that connects machine learning with real engineering systems and prepares me for applied research. My BEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Covenant University gave me a foundation in signals and systems, probability and statistics, linear algebra, control systems, and digital signal processing. I completed a final-year project on edge inference for low-cost power-quality sensors.

Since January 2024, I have worked as a machine-learning engineer at GridSense Africa, where I have built load-forecasting pipelines and anomaly-detection prototypes for distribution networks. This work has strengthened my interest in reliable machine learning for infrastructure and in methods that can operate under limited data and imperfect sensing conditions. I have also submitted the manuscript “Self-supervised event detection for weak distribution grids” to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid on 4 May 2026; no decision has been received.

My goal is to develop the theoretical and practical depth needed for applied machine-learning research, particularly for energy and other infrastructure systems. ETH Zürich’s data-science environment is a strong fit for this direction. I would bring an engineering perspective, experience with Python, PyTorch, embedded C, signal processing, and MLOps, and a commitment to careful, reproducible work.

I can self-fund tuition up to £18,000 and would need support above that amount. I have no disciplinary history.

observation.title: EMBL International PhD Programme – Unique in the world and waiting for you!
headings: Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research.
Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed
observation.text: European Molecular Biology Laboratory Home Directory Search EMBL International PhD Programme Unique in the world and waiting for you! Home Application Programme overview Why EMBL? Contact us Established in 1983, the EMBL International PhD Programme (EIPP) provides PhD students with an excellent starting platform for a successful career in science by fostering early independence and interdisciplinary research. EMBL is dedicated to promoting excellence in the molecular life sciences throughout Europe. To achieve this goal, we inspire and train talented young scientists to become skilled and creative future leaders in academia, industry and other sectors. The EIPP provides comprehensive interdisciplinary training, maintaining a careful balance between theory and practice, close mentoring and creative freedom, collaborative teamwork and independence. These key characteristics make the EIPP a role model, which has inspired similar programmes at research institutions throughout Europe and the world. The enriching encounter of different nationalities, the friendly and collaborative atmosphere, and the passion for science is what unites EMBL’s diverse staff and provides the ideal setting to forge long-lasting connections and make studying at EMBL a unique formative experience. Application Two recruitment rounds are organised each year across all EMBL sites. The application deadlines and all relevant information are published well in advance. Registration for the 2026 PhD Summer Recruitment is closed The next application round will open in September 2026. Programme Overview Explore the structure and content of the EMBL International PhD Programme. **Longer duration due to COVID-19 related delays. Research at EMBL Find out more about the cutting-edge Research Topics investigated across our different Research Units. The complexity of current biological research questions increasingly calls for interdisciplinary approaches. To prepare our students for this challenge, the EIPP puts great emphasis on bringing together different fields of expertise: we actively encourage candidates with backgrounds in chemistry, physics, mathematics, molecular medicine, computer science or engineering to apply and work closely with biologists to answer fundamental questions in life sciences. PHD Symposium Since its first edition in 2000, the annual EMBL International PhD Symposium in Heidelberg developed into a well-recognized and highly appreciated scientific event. It is always EMBL’s first year PhD students who take on the responsibility for the conceptual development and organization of the meeting. The symposia provide a great platform for networking and scientific exchange, featuring lectures by top-level scientists as well as plenty of opportunities for young researchers to present their work. See the full list of past symposia Upcoming symposium Shifting Gears — Automation, AI, and High-Throughput Methodologies 2 – 4 December 2026 EMBL Heidelberg Contact Monika Lachner Head of EICAT Brenda Stride Fellowship Programmes Lead and Deputy Head of Internal Scientific Training Anna Alasalmi Programme Officer / Training & Events Vera Beck Senior Programme Officer – Graduate Talent Acquisition Fulvio Grigolato Project and Programme Manager Martina Alice Candela Administrative Trainee EMBL Graduate Office EMBL Heidelberg Meyerhofstraße 1 69117 Heidelberg Germany Tel: +49 6221 387-8612/8896 Fax: +49 6221 387-8400 Email: graduate-office@embl.org EMBL is Europe’s life sciences laboratory – an intergovernmental organisation with more than 80 independent research groups covering the spectrum of molecular biology. observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD London, Bloomsbury The Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCL is one of the top departments in the UK for graduate study and has a broad range of bases for research in Physics of any UK university. A UCL Physics PhD provides evidence of the type of problem-solving skills which are an ideal qualification for a further career in research or the wider job market. UK students International students Study mode Full-time Part-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £6,400 Duration 3 academic years Programme starts October 2026 February 2027 May 2027 Applications accepted Applications are accepted on a rolling basis but should be submitted at least three months prior to your preferred start date. Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK integrated Master’s (MSci or MPhys) degree in a relevant discipline, or an undergraduate degree followed by an MSc in a relevant discipline, or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard. An upper second- or first-class UK Bachelor’s or equivalent may be considered in special circumstances. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 1 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. ATAS statement If you are intending to apply for a time-limited visa to complete your UCL studies (e.g. Student visa, Skilled worker visa, PBS dependant visa etc.) you may be required to obtain ATAS clearance. This will be confirmed to you if you obtain an offer of a place. Please note that ATAS processing times can take up to six months, so we recommend you consider these timelines when submitting your application to UCL. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. observation.title: Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD | Prospective Students Graduate - UCL – University College London
observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD London, Bloomsbury The Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCL is one of the top departments in the UK for graduate study and has a broad range of bases for research in Physics of any UK university. A UCL Physics PhD provides evidence of the type of problem-solving skills which are an ideal qualification for a further career in research or the wider job market. UK students International students Study mode Full-time Part-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £6,400 Duration 3 academic years Programme starts October 2026 February 2027 May 2027 Applications accepted Applications are accepted on a rolling basis but should be submitted at least three months prior to your preferred start date. Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK integrated Master’s (MSci or MPhys) degree in a relevant discipline, or an undergraduate degree followed by an MSc in a relevant discipline, or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard. An upper second- or first-class UK Bachelor’s or equivalent may be considered in special circumstances. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 1 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. ATAS statement If you are intending to apply for a time-limited visa to complete your UCL studies (e.g. Student visa, Skilled worker visa, PBS dependant visa etc.) you may be required to obtain ATAS clearance. This will be confirmed to you if you obtain an offer of a place. Please note that ATAS processing times can take up to six months, so we recommend you consider these timelines when submitting your application to UCL. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. observation.title: Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD | Prospective Students Graduate - UCL – University College London
observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD London, Bloomsbury The Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCL is one of the top departments in the UK for graduate study and has a broad range of bases for research in Physics of any UK university. A UCL Physics PhD provides evidence of the type of problem-solving skills which are an ideal qualification for a further career in research or the wider job market. UK students International students Study mode Full-time Part-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £6,400 Duration 3 academic years Programme starts October 2026 February 2027 May 2027 Applications accepted Applications are accepted on a rolling basis but should be submitted at least three months prior to your preferred start date. Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK integrated Master’s (MSci or MPhys) degree in a relevant discipline, or an undergraduate degree followed by an MSc in a relevant discipline, or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard. An upper second- or first-class UK Bachelor’s or equivalent may be considered in special circumstances. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 1 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. ATAS statement If you are intending to apply for a time-limited visa to complete your UCL studies (e.g. Student visa, Skilled worker visa, PBS dependant visa etc.) you may be required to obtain ATAS clearance. This will be confirmed to you if you obtain an offer of a place. Please note that ATAS processing times can take up to six months, so we recommend you consider these timelines when submitting your application to UCL. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Physics and Astronomy MPhil/PhD London, Bloomsbury The Department of Physics and Astronomy at UCL is one of the top departments in the UK for graduate study and has a broad range of bases for research in Physics of any UK university. A UCL Physics PhD provides evidence of the type of problem-solving skills which are an ideal qualification for a further career in research or the wider job market. UK students International students Study mode Full-time Part-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £6,400 Duration 3 academic years Programme starts October 2026 February 2027 May 2027 Applications accepted Applications are accepted on a rolling basis but should be submitted at least three months prior to your preferred start date. Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK integrated Master’s (MSci or MPhys) degree in a relevant discipline, or an undergraduate degree followed by an MSc in a relevant discipline, or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard. An upper second- or first-class UK Bachelor’s or equivalent may be considered in special circumstances. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 1 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. ATAS statement If you are intending to apply for a time-limited visa to complete your UCL studies (e.g. Student visa, Skilled worker visa, PBS dependant visa etc.) you may be required to obtain ATAS clearance. This will be confirmed to you if you obtain an offer of a place. Please note that ATAS processing times can take up to six months, so we recommend you consider these timelines when submitting your application to UCL. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. These techniques are employed in complex applications in natural science, engineering and social science. The specialized Master's degree programme in data science equips students with all relevant knowledge and skills while combining theoretical foundations with practical experience. A central part of the program is the Data Science Laboratory, where students tackle specific and practical problems of interdisciplinary applications. In this course students engage in all tasks - from the process modelling to the implementation and validation of data science techniques. Medicine, finance or environment: data science is used in most fields and thus enables graduates of the program to work in their industry of choice. Regardless of the industry, most large companies have data scientists working for or with them. A Data Science education emerges as one of the most valued academic competence in the information society of today. The Master in Data Science is a joint programme offered by the departments of Computer Science, Mathematics as well as Information Technology and Electrical Engineering. observation.text: Homepage Navigation Search Content Footer Contact Sitemap Header Main Navigation News & events ETH Zurich Studies at ETH Zurich Doctorate Research Industry & Knowledge Transfer Campus Search Departments ETH Zurich Select a department Departments D-ARCH: Architecture D-BAUG: Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering D-BSSE: Biosystems Science and Engineering D-INFK: Computer Science D-ITET: Information Technology and Electrical Engineering D-MATL: Department of Materials D-MAVT: Mechanical and Process Engineering D-BIOL: Biology D-CHAB: Chemistry and Applied Biosciences D-MATH: Mathematics D-PHYS: Physics D-EAPS: Earth and Planetary Sciences D-HEST: Health Sciences and Technology D-USYS: Environmental Systems Science D-MTEC: Management, Technology and Economics D-GESS: Humanities, Social and Political Sciences Language Selection en English Deutsch Français (TA) Italiano (TA) You are here Homepage Studies at ETH Zurich … Master’s degree studies Range of degree programmes Engineering Sciences Data Science Master Data Science Research in the field of data science requires solid skills in managing and storing massive amounts of data as well as the ability to develop efficient mathematical algorithms for data analysis. These techniques are employed in complex applications in natural science, engineering and social science. The specialized Master's degree programme in data science equips students with all relevant knowledge and skills while combining theoretical foundations with practical experience. A central part of the program is the Data Science Laboratory, where students tackle specific and practical problems of interdisciplinary applications. In this course students engage in all tasks - from the process modelling to the implementation and validation of data science techniques. Medicine, finance or environment: data science is used in most fields and thus enables graduates of the program to work in their industry of choice. Regardless of the industry, most large companies have data scientists working for or with them. A Data Science education emerges as one of the most valued academic competence in the information society of today. The Master in Data Science is a joint programme offered by the departments of Computer Science, Mathematics as well as Information Technology and Electrical Engineering. observation.text: Skip to main content Search Menu Home Computer Science MSc London, Bloomsbury Become a computer scientist in just one year through this conversion programme and enhance your career prospects in a growing and innovative field. The Computer Science MSc teaches everything from programming to app engineering while providing opportunities to create solutions for industrial or research clients. Taught at UCL, world-renowned for computer science research, this is an exceptional place to build your foundations as a computer scientist. UK students International students Study mode Full-time UK tuition fees (2026/27) £21,500 Duration 1 calendar year Programme starts September 2026 Applications accepted Applicants who require a visa: 20 Oct 2025 – 27 Mar 2026 Applications closed Applicants who do not require a visa: 20 Oct 2025 – 28 Aug 2026 Applications close at 10am UK time Applications open Apply for this course Entry requirements A minimum of an upper second-class UK Bachelor's degree (or international qualification of an equivalent standard) in a subject other than computer science or information technology. This includes subfields of Computer Science such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Software Engineering, among others. Evidence should be included within the application to demonstrate suitable mathematical skills (to at least Mathematics A-level standard), and analytical skills. Although the programme is intended for those who are new to Computer Science, applicants must ensure they have standard computational thinking skills, as programming is a core part of the programme. English language requirements The English language level for this course is: Level 2 UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. The courses will develop your academic English and academic skills required to succeed at postgraduate level. Further information can be found on our English language requirements page. Equivalent qualifications Country-specific information, including details of when UCL representatives are visiting your part of the world, can be obtained from the International Students website. International applicants can find out the equivalent qualification for their country by selecting from the list below. Please note that the equivalency will correspond to the broad UK degree classification stated on this page (e.g. upper second-class). Where a specific overall percentage is required in the UK qualification, the international equivalency will be higher than that stated below. Please contact Graduate Admissions should you require further advice. sections.title: Programme application deadline
sections.body: UCL Computer Science MSc, September 2026 entry: applicants requiring a visa had an application window of 20 October 2025–27 March 2026; the course page states applications are closed. Applicants not requiring a visa may apply until 28 August 2026 at 10:00 UK time. Because the applicant is a Nigerian citizen resident in Nigeria, the visa-required deadline is the relevant pathway unless UCL confirms otherwise. The page does not state a separate deadline timezone for the visa deadline; the non-visa closing time is explicitly 10:00 UK time. As of 8 August 2026, both the visa deadline and the programme's explicit scholarship deadline below have passed, while the non-visa admissions deadline remains future-dated but is not the expected route without confirmed visa exemption.

sections.title: Programme-linked funding
sections.body: The Computer Science MSc page lists the UCL East London Scholarship with a deadline of 25 June 2026. The dedicated official scholarship page specifies 5:00pm BST on Thursday 25 June 2026, covering tuition fees plus a £17,096 maintenance payment. It is restricted to Home fee-status applicants ordinarily resident in the UK or Ireland, with additional east-London residence/education and household-income criteria. The applicant's supplied Nigerian citizenship and Lagos residence do not establish eligibility and appear inconsistent with the published Home/UK-Ireland criterion; this should be treated as not eligible unless UCL confirms otherwise. The scholarship is not a general Computer Science MSc award.

sections.title: General UCL funding
sections.body: UCL's university-wide funding page directs postgraduate taught applicants to the UCL funding catalogue and Scholarships Finder; it does not publish one universal funding deadline. UCL separately advises students to investigate funding at least 12 months before the relevant academic year because individual scholarship deadlines vary. Therefore, no distinct general UCL funding deadline can be verified from the supplied official page. Individual awards must be checked separately by nationality, fee status, programme, and award-specific deadline.

sections.title: Important funding context
sections.body: The official course page lists 2026/27 overseas tuition fees of £42,700 for this MSc. The applicant's stated self-funding limit is £18,000, so the verified tuition shortfall is £24,700 before living costs, subject to fee-status confirmation and any award received.

sections.title: Unverified items / next check
sections.body: No separate Computer Science-specific international funding deadline was verified from the official pages supplied. The official Computer Science scholarships page points applicants to the UCL Scholarships Finder and general UCL funding site rather than publishing a single department-wide deadline. Recheck award-specific pages before any future application because deadlines and eligibility can change.

follow_ups: Confirm whether the applicant requires a UK Student visa; if yes, the 27 March 2026 programme deadline has passed.
Use the UCL Scholarships Finder to screen nationality- and fee-status-specific awards; record each award's own official deadline separately.
Confirm overseas fee status and funding plan given the £42,700 tuition fee and £18,000 self-funding ceiling.

content.text:
## Best-fit current EMBL group leaders

I found **two strong fits and one plausible adjacent fit** for Priya’s stated interests in single-cell analysis, host–pathogen biology, pathogen genomics, and reproducible computational workflows.

| Group leader | Current affiliation | Evidence of scientific fit | Evidence they are accepting PhD students |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wolfgang Huber** | Group Leader and Senior Scientist, **EMBL Heidelberg**; Huber Group | **Strongest computational fit.** His group develops methods for single-cell and spatial omics, CRISPR/drug perturbation data, and quantitative biology. EMBL’s Infection Biology pages specifically identify his work with single-cell omics, perturbation assays, and infectious-disease applications including **malaria and leptospirosis**. This aligns closely with Priya’s scRNA-seq, malaria, R/Python, and Bayesian-modelling background. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/people/person/wolfgang-huber/?utm_source=openai)) | **Not verified.** Huber does not appear in EMBL’s current preliminary list of groups actively recruiting for the 2026 Summer Recruitment. The list may change, but there is no official evidence located that his group is currently accepting students. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Nassos Typas** | Head of Molecular Systems Biology and Group Leader, **EMBL Heidelberg** | **Strong host–pathogen and microbial-systems fit.** The Typas group studies bacterial cellular networks, microbiomes, antibiotics, and host–pathogen interactions, including Salmonella infection and bacterial responses within host cells. Its work combines high-throughput genetics, sequencing, computational analysis, and reproducible systems approaches—highly relevant to Priya’s pathogen-genomics and Nextflow experience. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/typas/?utm_source=openai)) | **Not verified for the EIPP.** Typas is not listed among the current 2026 recruiting groups on EMBL’s official recruitment page. An EMBL project document shows a recent Typas-hosted project involving pathogen/commensal *E. coli*, microbiomes, sequencing pipelines, and Python/R, but that is evidence of a project opportunity—not proof of an open EIPP PhD position now. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Jordi van Gestel** | Group Leader, **EMBL Heidelberg**, Developmental Biology Unit / Microbial Ecosystems Transversal Theme | **Adjacent but genuine fit.** His group uses quantitative single-cell microscopy, functional genomics, CRISPR libraries, experimental evolution, and mathematical modelling to study microbial interactions and the evolution of host–symbiont or host–pathogen relationships. This fits Priya’s single-cell and reproducible computational interests, although the biological systems are presently more microbial ecology/predation than human infection or malaria. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/van-gestel/?utm_source=openai)) | **Not verified.** His group is not listed among the current 2026 EIPP recruiting groups, and I found no official current PhD vacancy on the group page. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |

## Recommendation

1. **Wolfgang Huber — highest overall fit**  
   Best match for Priya’s computational single-cell profile and malaria-related experience. A proposed project could focus on single-cell or spatial analysis of infected tissues, host-response heterogeneity, or perturbation-based host–pathogen modelling.

2. **Nassos Typas — strongest pathogen/microbial-systems fit**  
   Particularly suitable if Priya wants to move toward bacterial infection, microbiome–pathogen interactions, antimicrobial resistance, or genome-wide functional screens.

3. **Jordi van Gestel — exploratory third choice**  
   Worth considering if Priya is open to broader microbial host–pathogen evolution and single-cell experimental systems, but it is a less direct match than Huber or Typas for human infectious disease.

## Important distinction: fit versus student availability

The official EMBL recruitment page states that its recruiting-group list identifies groups **actively looking to hire PhD students**, but also warns that the list is preliminary and may change. Neither Huber, Typas, nor van Gestel appears on the current list I found. Therefore:

- **Scientific fit:** verified for all three from official EMBL group or programme pages.
- **Current acceptance of PhD students:** **not verified for any of the three**.
- The 2026 Summer Recruitment is closed; EMBL states that the next **2027 Winter Recruitment opens in September 2026**. The programme’s application process is centralised, and applicants indicate groups of interest rather than relying solely on individual informal recruitment. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai))

**Bottom line:** Priya should prioritise **Huber** and **Typas** as the two substantive fits, with **van Gestel** as a defensible third option. She should not describe any of them as “accepting students” unless EMBL’s next official recruiting-group list or a group-specific vacancy confirms it.

sections.title: Shortlist
sections.body:
1. Wolfgang Huber — strongest computational/single-cell fit. EMBL identifies him as Group Leader and Senior Scientist in Heidelberg. His group develops statistical and computational methods for single-cell and spatial omics, CRISPR/drug perturbation assays, quantitative imaging, and biomedical/clinical datasets. This directly matches Priya’s scRNA-seq, R/Python, Bayesian-modelling, and malaria-related profile. citeturn0search4turn0search9

2. Nassos Typas — strongest bacterial host–pathogen/microbial-systems fit. EMBL identifies him as Head of Molecular Systems Biology and Group Leader. His group studies bacterial cellular networks, sequencing-enabled genome-wide readouts, antibiotic resistance, and pathogenic or commensal bacteria in microbiomes. An official EMBL project description hosted by Typas specifically involves pathogenic/commensal E. coli, sequencing pipelines, metagenomics, Python/R, and machine learning. citeturn0search1turn0search10turn0search12

3. Jordi van Gestel — credible adjacent fit. EMBL identifies him as a Heidelberg Group Leader. His group combines quantitative single-cell microscopy, functional genomics, high-content CRISPR libraries, experimental evolution, and mathematical modelling to study microbial predator–prey and emerging host–symbiont/host–pathogen interactions. The match is less direct for human infection or malaria than Huber or Typas. citeturn0search2turn0search5

sections.title: Fit versus acceptance evidence
sections.body: The official EMBL International PhD Programme recruiting page says its listed groups are actively looking to hire PhD students and that the list is preliminary and may change. The current list includes the Typas Group but does not include the Huber Group or van Gestel Group. Therefore, current EIPP recruitment is verified for Typas at the programme-list level only; it is not verified for Huber or van Gestel. This does not establish that Typas has a project matching Priya’s exact interests, only that the group is currently listed as recruiting. citeturn0search0

sections.title: Programme timing
sections.body: EMBL’s official application page states that 2026 Summer Recruitment is closed and that the next 2027 Winter Recruitment opens in September 2026. The page also explains that applicants select groups of interest and that both recruiting and non-recruiting Group Leaders participate in the virtual panel assessment. citeturn0search7turn0search11

sections.title: Recommended ordering
sections.body: Prioritise Huber for computational single-cell and spatial-omics alignment; Typas for bacterial infection, microbiome, pathogen genomics, and current EIPP recruitment; and van Gestel as a broader microbial-interaction option. Do not state that Huber or van Gestel are accepting students. For Typas, state only that the group appears on EMBL’s current recruiting-group list, not that a specific project or supervisor slot is guaranteed.

follow_ups: Recheck EMBL’s recruiting-group page when the 2027 Winter Recruitment opens in September 2026.
If contacting groups later, ask whether a project involving single-cell host-response analysis or pathogen genomics is available within the relevant recruitment round.

content.text:
## Best current EMBL group-leader fits

I found **three current EMBL group leaders** whose research is relevant to Priya’s stated interests in computational biology, single-cell analysis, host–pathogen interactions, and reproducible genomics. The strongest overall fit is **Nassos Typas**, followed by **Oliver Stegle** and **Peer Bork**.

| Group leader | Current affiliation | Evidence of scientific fit | Evidence of accepting PhD students |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Nassos Typas** | Head of Molecular Systems Biology, EMBL Heidelberg | His group studies systems microbiology, bacterial cellular networks, microbiomes, and explicitly investigates the **host–pathogen interface**, including Salmonella infection, host responses, pathogen metabolism, and bacterial–phage interactions. This is the closest match to Priya’s host–pathogen goals, although the group’s work is more bacterial systems biology than single-cell host transcriptomics. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/typas/?utm_source=openai)) | **Strong evidence.** Typas is listed on EMBL’s current “Recruiting Group Leaders” page for the EMBL International PhD Programme. The page states that listed groups are actively looking to hire PhD students. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Oliver Stegle** | EMBL Heidelberg / DKFZ, Heidelberg | The Stegle group develops statistical and machine-learning methods for high-dimensional molecular data, including **single-cell**, spatial, and multi-omics data. This aligns very well with Priya’s scRNA-seq, Bayesian-modelling, R/Python, and reproducible computational-workflow background. The biological focus is broad rather than specifically infectious disease or host–pathogen biology. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/stegle/?utm_source=openai)) | **Strong evidence.** Stegle is listed among the current recruiting EMBL groups, and the group’s Join Us page specifically directs PhD applicants to the EMBL International PhD Programme. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Peer Bork** | Group Leader and Director of Scientific Activities, EMBL Heidelberg | The Bork group performs computational analysis of microbiome data across genes, proteins, cells, and microbial communities, using large-scale metagenomic and multi-omics datasets. Its work on microbial communities, disease biomarkers, drug–microbe interactions, and microbial ecology could support a host–microbiome or pathogen-genomics direction. The fit to single-cell host–pathogen work is indirect compared with Typas and Stegle. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/groups/bork/?utm_source=openai)) | **No verified current PhD-recruitment evidence found.** The current EMBL recruiting-group list does not list Bork, and the group’s open-positions page describes Bachelor’s/Master’s opportunities but does not establish an active PhD opening. Do not present Bork as currently accepting PhD students without direct confirmation. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/recruiting-group-leaders/?utm_source=openai)) |

### Recommended prioritisation

1. **Nassos Typas — highest thematic fit and current recruitment evidence.**  
   Best choice if Priya wants to connect computational genomics and single-cell expertise to bacterial infection, pathogen physiology, and host–pathogen systems.

2. **Oliver Stegle — strongest methods fit and current recruitment evidence.**  
   Best choice for a quantitatively focused PhD centred on single-cell/spatial analysis, statistical genetics, machine learning, and scalable workflows. A host–pathogen application would likely need to be developed through collaboration or a suitable project rather than assumed from the group’s core biological programme.

3. **Peer Bork — relevant computational microbiome alternative, but recruitment unverified.**  
   Worth considering for microbial community, microbiome, pathogen surveillance, and multi-omics work, but there is currently no official evidence that he is accepting PhD students in the relevant recruitment round.

### Programme and timing note

The EMBL International PhD Programme’s **2026 Summer Recruitment closed on March 9, 2026**. EMBL states that the next round, **2027 Winter Recruitment, opens in September 2026**. EMBL’s recruitment page also explains that applicants indicate research-group preferences, while recruiting Group Leaders review eligible applications and select candidates for interviews. ([embl.org](https://www.embl.org/about/info/embl-international-phd-programme/application/?utm_source=openai))

**Bottom line:** Priya should prioritise **Typas and Stegle** in the next EMBL application round. Bork is a scientifically plausible third option, but his student-acceptance status should be treated as **unknown**, not inferred from his affiliation or research profile.

content.text:
## Assessment: not currently verifiable as satisfying the prerequisite

**Conclusion:** Amara has a strong subject fit and relevant academic record, but the supplied materials do **not** establish that she satisfies UCL Physics and Astronomy’s current academic prerequisite. The main issue is that the programme expects preparation at approximately **Master’s level**, while the transcript shows only a BSc.

### Requirement reconciliation

| Requirement | Official current position | Applicant evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relevant discipline | UCL seeks a strong technical background such as Physics, with interest in Physics or Astronomy. | BSc Physics; Quantum Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Nuclear and Particle Physics, Computational Physics; detector research at CERN OpenLab. | **Satisfied on the available evidence** |
| Academic level | The formal entry requirement is normally an upper-second integrated UK Master’s, or an undergraduate degree followed by a relevant MSc, or equivalent overseas preparation. A Bachelor’s-equivalent may be considered only in special circumstances. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd)) | Four-year BSc Physics, CGPA 4.62/5.00. No MSc or integrated Master’s is documented. | **Not established** |
| Department-level qualification expectation | UCL’s “Who this course is for” section says applicants are generally expected to have a good UK Master’s equivalent and states that the programme will not accept candidates qualified only to Bachelor’s level. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd)) | The applicant is currently documented as Bachelor’s-qualified only. | **Likely unmet unless UCL confirms an exception** |
| English | This course requires UCL English Level 1. Nigerian nationality does not itself qualify for UCL’s listed majority-English-speaking-country exemption; evidence of English education or an accepted test is therefore needed unless UCL grants another exemption. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd)) | No English test, qualifying exemption, or UCL-confirmed medium-of-instruction evidence is supplied. | **Cannot verify** |
| References | The programme requires two references. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd)) | Professor Eze and Dr Marin appear potentially suitable; Mr Aina is less suitable because he did not see the applicant’s academic work. | **Potentially satisfiable; not yet verified** |
| Supervisor contact | UCL says applicants should generally identify and contact potential supervisors before applying. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd)) | No supervisor identified or contact evidence supplied. | **Cannot verify** |

### Academic and subject fit

The subject preparation is persuasive for the **High Energy Particle Physics** pathway: the applicant has a Physics degree, relevant nuclear/particle and computational coursework, a detector-focused undergraduate project, programming experience in Python and C++, ROOT and Geant4, and current CERN OpenLab research on charged-particle track reconstruction.

However, those strengths do not by themselves overcome the programme’s stated level requirement. UCL’s current page contains a general clause allowing a Bachelor’s-equivalent in “special circumstances,” but the same page separately states that it will not accept applicants qualified only to Bachelor’s level. The safer reconciliation is that a BSc-only applicant should be treated as **not meeting the normal prerequisite unless the department confirms an exceptional review in writing**. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd))

### What cannot be verified

1. **Whether the University of Lagos BSc and 4.62/5.00 CGPA are accepted as the required overseas equivalent.** UCL’s Nigeria page currently exposes only a country-information placeholder, so no usable official Nigerian equivalency value could be confirmed from that page. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/international/nigeria))  
2. **Whether the applicant qualifies for an English-language exemption** or must provide a Level 1 test result.  
3. **Whether UCL would treat the CERN research experience and submitted publication as a “special circumstance”** allowing consideration without an MSc. The official page does not define that exception.  
4. **Whether a suitable supervisor has agreed to consider the application.**  
5. **Funding:** UCL lists departmental/project studentships but does not establish that this applicant would receive full tuition and living support. The displayed China Scholarship Council–UCL award is marked closed for 2026/27. ([ucl.ac.uk](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/research-degrees/physics-and-astronomy-mphil-phd))

### Final determination

**Subject prerequisite:** likely satisfied.  
**Academic-level prerequisite:** **not satisfied on the current record / requires official exception confirmation**.  
**English prerequisite:** unverified.  
**Overall:** **Do not describe the applicant as currently eligible.** The appropriate status is **“strong subject fit, but academic prerequisite unresolved and potentially disqualifying.”**

The decisive next step would be to obtain written confirmation from UCL Physics and Astronomy or Graduate Admissions that this BSc-only profile may be considered under the programme’s special-circumstances provision.

sections.title: Verified prerequisite outcome
sections.body: Academic grade equivalency: provisionally met. UCL’s Nigeria country page lists a Bachelor’s degree with 63% or 3.75/5.0 as an upper-second equivalent; Amara’s transcript reports 4.62/5.00. However, the Physics and Astronomy programme requires an upper-second integrated Master’s, an undergraduate degree followed by a relevant MSc, or equivalent overseas preparation. Its course-specific guidance says it generally seeks a good UK Master’s equivalent and will not accept applicants qualified only to Bachelor’s level. Amara’s materials document a BSc only, so the decisive academic-level prerequisite is unresolved and likely unmet absent an official exception.

sections.title: Subject preparation
sections.body: The subject prerequisite is strongly supported: BSc Physics; Quantum Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Statistical Mechanics, Mathematical Methods, Nuclear and Particle Physics, and Computational Physics; a detector-focused Monte Carlo project; and current CERN OpenLab research involving charged-particle track reconstruction and uncertainty calibration.

sections.title: Other current requirements
sections.body: The course requires UCL English Level 1. Nigerian citizenship is not on UCL’s listed majority-English-speaking-country exemption list, and the materials contain no accepted recent test result or qualifying exemption evidence. Two references are required; Professor Eze and Dr Marin appear plausible candidates from the supplied facts, but no referee consent or submission evidence exists. UCL also generally expects applicants to identify and contact potential supervisors before applying; no such contact is documented.

sections.title: What cannot be verified
sections.body: It cannot be verified that UCL would accept the BSc-only profile under the programme’s special-circumstances clause; the official page does not define the exception. It also cannot be verified that the applicant has met English Level 1, identified an agreeing supervisor, or secured full tuition and living funding. The 2026/27 China Scholarship Council–UCL Joint Research Scholarship is officially marked closed.

follow_ups: Obtain written confirmation from UCL Physics and Astronomy or Graduate Admissions that the BSc-only profile may be considered under special circumstances.

sections.title: Official rule
sections.body: The official LSE Master of Public Policy page states that applicants must have at least five years of policy-relevant experience, although exceptions may be granted for outstanding candidates with slightly less experience. It also describes the programme as designed for mid-career professionals with more than five years’ experience. Therefore, five years is a formal stated admissions expectation with a discretionary exception—not simply a preference used only to rank otherwise eligible applicants.

sections.title: Applicant’s roles
sections.body: The authorised employment history records policy analyst work at the Accra Metropolitan Research Unit from September 5, 2022 to December 15, 2023, and research assistant work at the Institute for Fiscal Studies from March 4, 2024 to the present. On August 8, 2026, these periods total approximately 3 years 8 months, excluding the documented December 16, 2023–March 3, 2024 transition gap. Both roles appear substantively policy-relevant based on the CV’s description of municipal revenue, social-protection targeting, and quasi-experimental evaluation work.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: The roles can plausibly be presented as relevant professional policy experience, but they do not satisfy the ordinary five-year threshold. Lena would need to rely on LSE’s stated exception for an outstanding candidate with slightly less experience. Her First Class BA, 3.78/4.00 GPA, strong quantitative coursework, Dean’s Award, and applied policy research record are potentially relevant strengths, but the official source does not guarantee that these facts will secure an exception. The appropriate classification is: standard experience expectation not met; possible discretionary exception; not an automatic eligibility pass.

follow_ups: If applying, explicitly explain the policy impact and quantitative content of both roles and ask LSE SPP whether approximately 3 years 8 months would be considered within its 'slightly less experience' exception.

observation.text: Skip to main content Current students Staff Alumni & friends Study Research Student life News & events About LSE Search Graduate (Taught) Application code: L4UT School of Public Policy Master of Public Policy Take the next step in your career as a policy leader. Develop your skills and confidence to tackle complex public policy challenges. Register your interest How to apply Overview Entry requirements Programme content Why study with us Your application Fees and funding Learning and assessment Graduate destinations Key information Study mode / Programme availability Home full-time students (9 months) Closed Overseas full-time students (9 months) Closed Academic year 2026/27 Start date September 2026 Location Houghton Street, London Application deadline Rolling admissions. Early application deadline: 22 January 2026. Register your interest How to apply Discover the Master of Public Policy at LSE Overview Introduction Introduction Designed for mid-career professionals with more than five years experience, this intensive nine-month programme brings together a global cohort to develop new perspectives and explore approaches to policy through theory and practical training. With an emphasis on developing an understanding of the components which form the craft of government, you’ll delve into topics such as policy analysis, economics and political science, drawing on world-leading expertise from across LSE. You’ll also develop your understanding of the public management profession, and the tools and approaches needed to enhance and reform public service provision. The broad-ranging curriculum gives you the flexibility to specialise in your chosen area of interest. The Master of Public Policy (MPP) attracts students from many different nationalities and professional backgrounds. So, you’ll study alongside peers with diverse policy experience – providing a rich learning experience to develop a truly global perspective on policy. You’ll also benefit from the School of Public Policy (SPP)’s emphasis on placing policy in practice through our regular seminar events with policy practitioners, and our Professional Skills Accelerator as well as SPP alumni career Q&As and mentorship scheme. This enables you to apply your learning to real-world scenarios and extend your professional network. Our graduates return to their professions equipped and confident to take on complex policy challenges in government, NGOs, think tanks and international organisations. LSE is rated number one in the UK for Social Policy (Good University Guide 2026). We were also awarded the highest UK ranking for research in the field of social policy in the most recent Research Excellence Framework (2021). So, you’ll be studying in a vibrant, highly rated research environment. Attend a recruitment event Entry requirements Upper second class honours (2:1) degree or equivalent in any discipline. Applicants must have at least five years of policy-relevant experience, though exceptions may be granted for outstanding candidates with slightly less experience. Please select your country from the dropdown list below to find out the entry requirements that apply to you. Who should apply? We welcome applications from individuals from a range of academic disciplines and professional backgrounds (with at least five years experience) who can demonstrate a passion for public policy and making a positive impact. Excellent candidates will possess a strong academic record and be able to demonstrate a commitment to public service as well as a clear understanding of the MPP and how they'll benefit from the programme. Whilst the MPP programme is designed to provide rigorous training in areas of econometrics and quantitative methods, there will be opportunities for individuals with less experience in these areas to develop or refresh their skills via online learning materials prior to the programme starting.
